description: The RETRY phrase (ISO 14.7.9; RETRY n TIMES | FOR n SECONDS | FOREVER on OPEN/READ/WRITE/REWRITE/DELETE) - an exhausted retry lands the CONFLICT'S OWN 9.1.13 status: n TIMES loops the lock check then reports 51/61/62 (GR1; a zero or negative n makes no further attempt, GR4a), FOR n SECONDS makes none because GR2 clamps the timeout period to this implementation's maximum meaningful value of zero (A.1 item 166) and reports the same, and FOREVER alone reports the 9.1.13.8 item 2 deadlock 52 - and only for a RECORD conflict, since 9.1.13.9 defines no deadlock value. A conflict held OUTSIDE the run unit (another run unit's handle) can clear: TIMES waits 100 ms before each re-attempt against it (A.1 item 165) and FOREVER keeps attempting until the operation completes (GR3). 2002 introduction; 0900 below 2002.
citation: ISO §2023:14.7.9 (OPEN/READ/WRITE/REWRITE/DELETE; RETRY n TIMES | FOR n SECONDS | FOREVER) — §2023:14.7.9.3 GR1 loops the registry check, GR2's SECONDS period is clamped to the A.1 item 166 maximum meaningful value of zero, GR4 a) screens a negative or zero amount, and only GR3's FOREVER reports the §2023:9.1.13.8 item 2 deadlock '52'; 2002 introduction
vcr: 2002 introduction (derive from the 2002 standard - Annex E covers 2014->2023 only)

IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. ROWRT.
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
       FILE-CONTROL.
           SELECT F ASSIGN TO "f.dat" ORGANIZATION IS SEQUENTIAL.
       DATA DIVISION.
       FILE SECTION.
       FD F.
       01 R PIC X(8).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           OPEN INPUT RETRY 3 TIMES F.
           CLOSE F.
           STOP RUN.
